summary: Defines the describes link relation type, which lets a resource representation indicate that it describes another resource. It is the opposite direction of the describedby relation. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: The describes link relation lets a description resource point to the resource it describes. The link says nothing about whether the description is trustworthy.

subtitle: A link relation for a resource that provides a description of another resource.

tldr.problem: The registered describedby relation points from a described resource to its description, but applications may need the reverse direction.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers describes: a link from resource A to B asserts that A provides a description of B.
tldr.outcome: The relation works across formats and identifiers, but does not establish that a description is accurate or authoritative.

today: RFC 6892 is an Informational registration of the describes link relation. The unit metadata lists no update or replacement.

sections.title: Describes and Describedby
sections.content:
Web applications use link relation types to express relationships between resources. RFC 6892 registers describes as the inverse of the existing describedby relation.

If resource A “describes” resource B, then A provides a description of B. The relation does not constrain the identifiers, formats, or representations of either resource.
sections.plainLanguage: A resource can link to another and say that it describes it. This is the reverse direction of describedby.

sections.title: Description Resources and Chains
sections.content:
The memo gives a use case in which a server hosts description resources and uses describes links to associate them with the resources they describe. The descriptions might use RDF, XML, JSON, or another representation.

Applications may also build chains of describes or describedby links. The RFC does not limit how many levels of description a chain may contain.
sections.plainLanguage: A service can link a description back to the resource it explains, in any supported format. Applications may connect several layers of descriptions.

sections.title: Trust and Authority
sections.content:
A describes link does not say that its source or target is authoritative. Resources can have multiple descriptions, including conflicting ones, and the relation makes no claim about the accuracy of a description.

Clients need a separate trust and security framework to assess both the description and the party that created the association.
sections.plainLanguage: A link does not prove that a description is correct. Clients need other ways to judge who supplied it and whether to trust it.
